extracted.intended_audience: Editors-in-Chief and journal editors who handle manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and expectations for Editors‑in‑Chief (and handling editors) on editorial policies, manuscript handling (peer review and decision making), conflicts of interest, and post‑publication issues. The page is a course overview introducing the Journal Editors' Code of Conduct and related practical guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure the journal publishes good quality research
rubrics_metrics.description: In one respect the role of an Editor-in-Chief is fairly straightforward: to ensure that the journal publishes good quality research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The position is multi-faceted and requires Editors-in-Chief to perform a variety of tasks and interact with a wide range of people; this overarching responsibility underpins other specific duties covered by the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand the basic principles of editorial policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course takes you through the fundamental concepts of the Journal Editors' Code of Conduct to ensure you understand editorial policy principles (no detailed policies provided on this page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript handling (including peer review and decision making)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper handling of manuscripts — including managing peer review and making editorial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course content includes manuscript handling (including peer review and decision making) and presents interactive questions and exercises to challenge editors on navigating difficult situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest (identification and management)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise and appropriately manage conflicts of interest in editorial processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts of interest are covered as a fundamental concept; related guidance appears across the course and linked modules (e.g., Fundamentals of Peer Review covers confidentiality and conflicts of interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Libellous and defamatory material (identification and handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify libellous or defamatory content and take appropriate action to avoid publication of such material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code includes content on libellous and defamatory material as an editorial responsibility; the course will present scenarios to test understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-specific policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of and apply policies that are specific to particular research fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code and course address field-specific policies as part of good editorial practice; editors should apply appropriate discipline-specific rules where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage issues arising after publication (e.g., corrections, retractions, expressions of concern).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-publication issues are listed as a topic area in the course; editors are expected to understand procedures for handling them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain confidentiality of manuscripts and reviewer identities where required by journal policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamentals of Peer Review course outlines basics of peer review, including confidentiality and conflicts of interest, and how these interact with reviewer selection and report assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify characteristics of a good reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise what makes a good peer reviewer for a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fundamentals of Peer Review course explains characteristics to look for when selecting reviewers (page references this as an instructional topic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inviting reviewers (best practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate processes and best practice for inviting reviewers to assess manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course covers how to invite reviewers as part of the peer review workflow; flowcharts and template letters are available in Editor Resources to assist with invitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess peer review reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the quality and usefulness of submitted peer review reports to inform editorial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fundamentals of Peer Review course describes how to assess peer review reports; interactive exercises help editors practise this skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics approval requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure manuscripts include necessary ethics approvals where human-subjects research or other regulated work is involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Ethics course content covers ethics approval requirements as a key editorial check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent to participate in research
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that studies involving human participants report appropriate informed consent procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Research Ethics topics; editors should check for statements about informed consent in submitted manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics requirements for animal studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm that animal studies meet ethical requirements and report relevant approvals and welfare considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Ethics module flags animal study ethics as an editorial responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial registration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Require and verify registration of clinical trials where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Research Ethics course includes clinical trial registration as a requirement editors should check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism: types, detection and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand different types of plagiarism, how to detect them, and appropriate editorial actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Plagiarism course covers different types of plagiarism, practicalities of using Crossref Similarity Check, and how to assess and take action on text overlap detected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Crossref Similarity Check / iThenticate (IRR service)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use similarity-checking tools and optional IRR (iThenticate Report & Response) service to analyse text overlap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IRR service analyses the Crossref Similarity Report and provides editors with a recommendation for new submissions; practical guidance on using these tools is provided in the Plagiarism/IRR materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and take action on text overlap detected
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate similarity reports and determine appropriate editorial responses to detected text overlap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Plagiarism module and IRR service offer guidance on interpreting similarity reports and recommended actions (e.g., queries to authors, rejection, correction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of flowcharts and template letters for common editorial problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply provided flowcharts and template letters to handle common editorial problems and situations according to best practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor Resources include flowcharts and template letters to help editors follow best-practice procedures when resolving issues.
